themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street signage failures have spiked dramatically this week and last week—missing signs up 433% (4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average) and dangling signs up 700% (3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average)—signaling potential systemic street maintenance breakdown in Kingsbridge/Bedford Park.
evidence: Street Sign - Missing: 4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (UP 433%, z-score: 3.92)
Street Sign - Dangling: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (UP 700%, z-score: 3.77)
Both spikes represent statistically significant deviations in a low-baseline category, suggesting concentrated recent failures rather than noise
reporting_angles: Walk the district to document missing/dangling signs; interview DOT about maintenance schedules and budget constraints
Check whether similar spikes are appearing in adjacent districts or citywide—is this a sign maintenance crisis?

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures Spiking
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints have jumped 134% this week compared to the 8-week baseline (34 complaints last week vs. 14.5 weekly average), affecting building access for residents and raising safety/accessibility concerns in a district with aging multifamily housing stock.
evidence: Elevator complaints: 34 last week vs. 14.5 weekly average (UP 134%, z-score: 5.69, high severity)
Spike is recent and sustained, not a one-week anomaly
District has significant public housing and older residential buildings where elevator downtime creates immediate accessibility crises
reporting_angles: Interview residents in buildings with broken elevators—focus on elderly, disabled, and families with strollers; document wait times and workarounds
Request DOB data on elevator violations and maintenance complaints filed against specific properties; identify chronic offenders

themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints surged 264% this week (15 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly average), suggesting either a crackdown by enforcement agencies or a sudden influx of unregistered vendors creating conflicts with residents.
evidence: Vendor Enforcement complaints: 15 THIS WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly average (UP 264%, z-score: 4.23, high severity)
This is the most recent spike signal in the dataset, appearing only in the current week
Could indicate either city enforcement action or grass-roots resident complaints about street vendor encroachment
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY and local enforcement agencies to ask if they initiated a targeted vendor compliance sweep this week
Interview residents and local business owners about vendor density and whether disputes have escalated recently

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Complaints Drop Unexpectedly
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints fell 42% this week (56 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 97.1 weekly average), a statistically significant improvement that may reflect recent enforcement action, resident disengagement, or data reporting lag—warrants clarification.
evidence: Unsanitary Condition complaints: 56 THIS WEEK vs. 97.1 weekly average (DOWN 42%, z-score: -5.5, high severity)
Statistically significant shift in opposite direction from other indicators
Despite long-running high volume of heat/hot water complaints (8,665 over 90 days), sanitation conditions have improved noticeably this week
reporting_angles: Ask DSNY and HPD if new sanitation or rat-control initiatives launched this week
Monitor whether this trend persists or reverses; confirm via street observations rather than relying solely on complaint data

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Infrastructure Stress
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped 279% last week (9 complaints vs. 2.4 weekly average), suggesting potential garbage collection delays, contamination issues, or resident behavior changes affecting waste management in the district.
evidence: Residential Disposal Complaint: 9 last week vs. 2.4 weekly average (UP 279%, z-score: 3.68, high severity)
Spike is recent (last week) and distinct from general sanitation trend, indicating targeted disposal-system stress
Complements broader unsanitary condition patterns observed over 90-day period
reporting_angles: Check DSNY schedules for collection delays or service changes in Kingsbridge/Bedford Park last week
Interview residents about compactor/dumpster access issues; photograph overfilled waste receptacles
